meaning: Mitsukurina, -ina (Latin) “belonging to” Kakichi Mitsukuri (1858–1909), University of Tokyo zoologist who had the holotype identified and described; owstoni, in honor of Alan Owston (1853–1915), English businessman, collector of Asian wildlife and resident of Yokohama, who secured the holotype from a fisherman (named for Owston at Mitsukuri's request)
description: A pale pink, soft-bodied deep-sea shark with a long, flat, blade-like snout and small rounded fins. Its jaws can shoot forward to snap up prey, showing long, narrow teeth, and its tail has a long upper lobe with almost no lower lobe. It is rarely seen alive, and was first described in 1898 from a specimen obtained in Japan.
depth: Mostly 270 to 960 m, recorded down to about 1,300 m
